1.  In this case, a Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred as DAR) was filed by IO Ombir Singh in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, which is treated as Claim Petition under Section 166 (1) read with Section 166 (4) MV Act.

1 It pertains to alleged accident of injured Wasim Ahmad (hereinafter referred as claimant), by vehicle bearing Reg. No.
HR 55L 9232 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), which was driven & owned by Vijender Singh (hereinafter referred as R-1) and insured with Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd (hereinafter referred as R-2).
2. Preliminary information about the accident was received on 13.04.2017 recorded vide DD no.03 at PS Sun Light Colony.
In response to which, ASI Ombir Singh along with Ct. Arun rushed to the spot at NH -24, near Hanuman Mandir (hereinafter referred as spot of accident) where they were informed that injured has already been rushed to hospital. Accidental Taxi bearing Registration No. DL 1RY 4687 and JCB bearing no. HR 55L 9232 were found parked at the spot which were shifted to the police station with the help of crane. Information about MLC of Wasim Ahmad, was received from LNJP wherein he was found admitted but was not in a medical fit state to make statement. 
Subsequently, on 18.04.2017, he came to police station and his statement with respect to occurrence of accident and his injuries was recorded. He narrated that he was a driver by profession and run vehicle bearing no. DL 1RY 4687 for Meru Cab Company. 
MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 2 of 35  He stated that his taxi was hit by offending vehicle, a JCB, on Yamuna Bridge, enroute airport from Indirapuram, when it took a sudden U-turn speedily and negligently, thereby his vehicle which caused injuries on his face and right foot. He also revealed the name of JCB driver as Vijender Singh and held him responsible for rash and negligent driving of such JCB Machine causing accident. FIR was registered on the basis of statement of Wasim. Statement u/s 161 Cr.PC was recorded. The accident vehicles were taken into police possession. Relevant documents were collected, result on MLC was also obtained. Driver of offending vehicle was arrested. It was revealed that vehicle was no valid fitness on the date of accident and therefore relevant penal provisions u/s 56/192 MV Act were added. Upon conclusion of investigation, Charge-sheet u/s 279/338 IPC,
56/192 MV Act was filed before Ld. Ilaka MM while DAR was filed in the Tribunal for adjudicating the compensation under Motor Vehicles Act. 
Proceedings:
3. All the contesting parties appeared before the court. Reply/
WS was filed by both the respondents respectively. 
Reply:
4. In the WS filed on behalf of driver cum owner, it is stated that accident did not take place on account of his rash and negligent driving. He clarified that he was driving the vehicle as Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
2 per the traffic norms but the claimant suddenly came in way of JCB Machine and accident happened. All the other allegations MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 3 of 35  were generally denied. 
5. In reply filed by Insurance Company, it is pointed that there is an unexplained delay of 4 days in lodging the FIR. 
Further, the driver of the taxi was not holding the valid and effective driving license. Further he was not even wearing a seat belt at the time of accident. It is also stated that the vehicle was being plied without fitness which constitute breach of terms of policy in question and therefore liability would solely fall upon the owner of the offending vehicle. It is further submitted that the accident occurred on account of fault and negligence of the taxi driver. It is further submitted that the insurance policy is an Act Only Policy which has not been issued for Third Party. It is accordingly prayed that the R-2 may be exonerated from its liability. 
Issues:
6. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed order dated 09.10.2017:
 i). Whether the injured Waseem suffered injuries in a road  traffic accident on 13.04.2017 due to rash and negligent  driving of vehicle bearing no. HR 55L 9232 driven and  owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP.
 ii). Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so,
 to what extent and from whom?OPP  iii). Relief.

7. Matter was then listed for Petitioner's Evidence. However MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 4 of 35  same was not led despite repeated opportunities. Interest being accrued to the claimant was also directed to be closed vide order dated 21.03.2018 since the date of framing of issues on 09.10.2017 till the evidence is led. Subsequently, claimant stopped appearing in the matter. The matter was eventually dismissed in default for non appearance as well as for non prosecution vide order dated 24.02.2021. 
Restoration of case:
8. An application for restoration was filed on 07.02.2023 Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
3 which was allowed vide order dated 09.10.2023 and the matter was restored to its original number and stage. 
Disability Assessment:
9. Counsel for the claimant filed an application for assessment of physical disability which was allowed and a Disability Assessment Certificate with 03% permanent physical impairment in relation to right foot was received from Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital as noted in the order dated 10.01.2024. 
Evidence:
10. On 12.02.2024, PW-1 appeared in the witness box and tendered his evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW1/A and relied upon his medical documents as Ex.PW1/1 (colly) and DAR as Ex.PW1/2. He was put to cross examination by counsel for the R-1 as well as by counsel for R-2. PE was closed upon request vide order dated 13.02.2024. Thereafter, matter was listed for RE which was also closed upon submission made by counsel for R-1 MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 5 of 35  & R-2 respectively that they do not want to lead any evidence as noted in the order dated 20.02.2024. 
Arguments:
11. Final Arguments were advanced on the same date. Brief Written Submissions were also filed by counsel for the claimant on the same date. 
12. On the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under :
 Issue No.1  Whether the injured Waseem suffered injuries in a road  traffic accident on 13.04.2017 due to rash and negligent  driving of vehicle bearing no. HR 55L 9232 driven and  owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP. 
13. What is required to be ascertained is whether rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle was responsible for sustaining injury by injured. 
14. It has been held in catena of cases that negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable (support drawn from the case of Bimla Devi & Ors Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
4 vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [ ( 2009 ) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. 
MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 6 of 35  Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287]. 
15. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under Section 279 &
338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of charge-sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 
16. It is also settled that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him as observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3)
AD Delhi 310.
17. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. 
18. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1/ injured person, it is noted that PW-1/Victim/Injured person deposed on the lines of original complaint/stand, which is already noted above. It was further deposed that the accident was attributed to rash and negligent driving of the R-1/ driver cum owner as he took U-turn suddenly at a high speed without blowing any horn, neglecting the traffic rules, there upon hitting the taxi. 
MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 7 of 35  19. The accident as such has not been denied by any of the respondents. The information about occurrence of offence was forthwith received and recorded vide DD entry. Both the accidental vehicles were found at the spot by ASI Ombir Singh who was assigned the said DD entry. It is mentioned in the FIR itself that the injured Wasim Ahmad who was the taxi driver was found admitted in LNJP Hospital, information about whose MLC was also separately received and registered. It is also part of record that the injured was medically not opined to be in a fit state to give the statement which is why the statement could not be immediately recorded by ASI Ombir Singh in the hospital. 
Statement of injured Wasim Ahmad was got recorded on 18.04.2017 when he himself visited the police station on the Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
5 basis of which, FIR was then registered. MLC is also filed as part of DAR which shows the date and hour of arrival and examination of injured Wasim Ahmad as 13.04.2017 at 01:57 AM which also substantiate the occurrence of accident and injuries sustained by injured in an accident. It is also noted that injured was rushed to the hospital by Sumit Kumar, B-12 CATS which shows that injured was rushed to hospital in CATS Ambulance. It cannot be stated that there was deliberate delay on the part of injured Wasim Ahmad in the registration of FIR. 
There is nothing to suggest that the information was intentionally withheld to draw any benefit or to concoct any story. The criminal law was put into motion right after the accident and Independent Law Enforcement Agencies were seized of the matter even though, formal complaint narrating the manner of MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 8 of 35  accident could not be recorded for plausible reasons. MLC duly records that there was dental injuries sustained by injured which substantiate his assertion that he was not in a position to speak, to be able to narrate the occurrence in detail. There is no dispute with respect to identification of the injured or the involvement of the two vehicles in the accident or the identification of driver cum owner of the offending vehicle. The driver cum owner has generally denied his negligence but has not disputed that he was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident. 
20. As noted earlier, Respondent no.1 has just made a bald denial of his negligent driving at the time of accident as the cause of accident but has not clarified as to how, he was justified in taking a sudden and speedy U-turn without caring for the straight traffic plying on the road. He has only stated that he duly followed the traffic norms but has not made any clarification on his part on the contextual circumstances detailed in the Tehrir of claimant. Again as earlier noted, he chose not to lead any evidence to clarify that he did not take any U-turn speedily or suddenly and that he honked before taking a U-turn or that he gave some indication to the straight traffic plying on the road that he was about to take u-turn or that he stopped at the turn to ascertain whether any traffic was coming straight which needed to be stopped or which needed to be given its way so as to negotiate a safe U-turn. As such the vehicle plying straight had to the first right to way and it was a duty on the part of vehicle which wanted to negotiate a right-turn to stop and see as to whether any vehicle was coming straight or not. Site plan, has MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 9 of 35  been filed as part of DAR which shows that the accidental taxi was plying straight on the road and was moving in its way whereas the offending vehicle took a right turn to come on the road and therefore, it was incumbent upon the offending vehicle Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
6 to ascertain and to adjudge the movement as well as speed of any vehicle plying straight. Mechanical Inspection Report of the accidental also show fresh damages on account of impact of the accident on both the accidental vehicles. PW-1 appeared in the witness box and was cross examined by counsel for R-1 wherein he asserted that the offending vehicle was moving in fast speed. 
He also clarified that even though, it was night when accident occurred but it was not dark and therefore, it cannot be inferred that the accident happened on account of low or unclear visibility which might have misled the offending vehicle or the accidental vehicle. There is no assertion on the part of R-1 that the accidental vehicle was running at high speed. There is no suggestion on the part of counsel for R-1 that the accident occurred on account of unmindful driving or reckless driving on the part of injured himself. 
21. Injured was also put to cross examination by counsel for the insurance company who did not put any question with respect to the factual details of the accident and only suggested that the accident occurred as injured was sleeping and was caused by some unknown vehicle which was categorically denied by the injured. 
22. Counsel for both the respondents could not elicit any contradiction in the testimony of injured and therefore, there is MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 10 of 35  no reason on record as to why his testimony should be discarded or not considered credit worthy. As such, it is settled that this issue has to be decided on the scales of preponderance of probabilities and any fishing or roving enquiry is not required to be undertaken into the negligence of the offending vehicle. 
23. Counsel for the insurance company has stated that contributory negligence must be deducted in this matter considering that the taxi had hit the JCB from behind and could not manage to keep a safe distance while driving thereby faulted in his duty to exercise due care and caution in driving a commercial vehicle on a public road. In this case as discussed above, the collision happened when JCB was trying to negotiate a turn while taxi was running straight on the road therefore, there is no occasion to consider managing a safe distance between two vehicles plying in the same directions on the road. The aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle has already been held into. There is nothing to suggest that taxi driver was running at a very high speed and could not control the vehicle. It appears that he could not decipher and anticipate the sudden turning of JCB which resulted in the collision. Therefore the submissions made by counsel for insurance company are not sustainable and hence rejected. 
24. As such, in view of the above analysis of material on record, evidence proved on record, charge-sheet against R-1, it is Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
7 held that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner. 
MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 11 of 35  ISSUE NO. 2  "Whether the injured is entitled to any  compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
 OPP"
25. Sec. 168 MV Act enjoins the Claim Tribunals to hold an enquiry into the claim to make an effort determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable. 
Same is reproduced hereunder for ready reference:
 "(1) Award of the Claims Tribunal.--On receipt of an  application for compensation made under section 166,
 the Claims Tribunal shall, after giving notice of the  application to the insurer and after giving the parties  (including the insurer) an opportunity of being heard,
 hold an inquiry into the claim or, as the case may be,
 each of the claims and, subject to the provisions of section 162 may make an award determining the  amount of compensation which appears to it to be just  and specifying the person or persons to whom  compensation shall be paid and in making the award  the Claims Tribunal shall specify the amount which  shall be paid by the insurer or owner or driver of the  vehicle involved in the accident or by all or any of  them, as the case may be: Provided that where such  application makes a claim for compensation under  section 140 in respect of the death or permanent  disablement of any person, such claim and any other  claim (whether made in such application or otherwise)
 for compensation in respect of such death or  permanent disablement shall be disposed of in  accordance with the provisions of Chapter X.
 (2) The Claims Tribunal shall arrange to deliver  copies of the award to the parties concerned  expeditiously and in any case within a period of fifteen  days from the date of the award.
 (3) When an award is made under this section, the MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 12 of 35  person who is required to pay any amount in terms of  such award shall, within thirty days of the date of  announcing the award by the Claims Tribunal, deposit  the entire amount awarded in such manner as the  Claims Tribunal may direct." 
26. Before putting in frame the position of law, it is noted that Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
8 the process of determining the compensation by the court is essentially a very difficult task and can never be an exact science. 
Perfect compensation is hardly possible, more so in claims of injury and disability. (As observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd, SLP (Civil) No. 19277 of 2019. 
27. The basic principle in assessing motor vehic compensation claims, is to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in before the accident, with other compensatory directions for loss of amenities and other payments. These general principles have been stated and reiterated in several decisions. [Support drawn from Govind Yadav v. New India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2011) 10 SCC 683.] 
28. This Tribunal has been tasked with determination of just compensation. The observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Divisional Controller, KSRTC v. Mahadeva Shetty and Another, (2003) 7 SCC 197, needs mention here (para 15): 
 "Statutory provisions clearly indicate that the  compensation must be "just" and it cannot be a  bonanza; not a source of profit but the same should  not be a pittance. The courts and tribunals have a  duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 13 of 35  amount of compensation, which should be just. What  would be "just" compensation is a vexed question. 
 There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases  for measuring the value of human life or a limb. 
 Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise  mathematical calculations. It would depend upon the  particular facts and circumstances, and attending  peculiar or special features, if any. Every method or  mode adopted for assessing compensation has to be  considered in the background of "just" compensation  which is the pivotal consideration. Though by use of  the expression "which appears to it to be just", a  wide discretion is vested in the Tribunal, the  determination has to be rational, to be done by a  judicious approach and not the outcome of whims,
 wild guesses and arbitrariness.. ..."
29. Delineating the damages as pecuniary and non pecuniary,
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case of R. D. Hattangadi Vs.
Pest Control (India) Pvt Ltd, 1995 AIR 755, made following observations:
 "9....while fixing an amount of compensation  payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
9  to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and  special damages. Pecuniary damages are those  which the victim has actually incurred and which are  capable of being calculated in terms of money;
 whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are  incapable of being assessed by arithmetical  calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts  pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by  the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of  earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other  material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are  concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental  and physical shock, pain and suffering, already  suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii)
 damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 14 of 35  life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on  account of injury the claimant may not be able to  walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of  expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the  normal longevity of the person concerned is  shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship, discomfort,
 disappointment, frustration and mental stress in life."
30. Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr.,
(2011) 1 SCC 343, by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. 
Following observations are relevant in the context:
 "40.General principles relating to compensation in  injury cases  5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988  ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award  must be just, which means that compensation should,
 to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the  claimant to the position prior to the accident. The  object of awarding damages is to make good the loss  suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money  can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 
 The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the  damages objectively and exclude from consideration  any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture  with reference to the nature of disability and its  consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be  compensated for the physical injury, but also for the  loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This  means that he is to be compensated for his inability  to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal  amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the  injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used  to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania  Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
10  1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control  (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri)
MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 15 of 35  250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970)
 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .]
 6. The heads under which compensation is awarded  in personal injury cases are the following:
 Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation,
 medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and  miscellaneous expenditure. 
 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the  injured would have made had he not been injured,
 comprising:
 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
 (b) Loss of future earnings on account of  permanent disability. 
 (iii) Future medical expenses. 
 Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
 (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a  consequence of the injuries. 
 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of  marriage).
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of  normal longevity).
 In routine personal injury cases, compensation will  be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv). It  is only in serious cases of injury, where there is  specific medical evidence corroborating the  evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be  granted under any of the heads (ii)(b),
 (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings  on account of permanent disability, future medical  expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of  life.
 7. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and  under Item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they  involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 16 of 35  ascertainable from the evidence. Award under the head  of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon  specific medical evidence regarding need for further  treatment and cost thereof. Assessment of non-pecuniary  damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves  determination of lump sum amounts with reference to  circumstances such as age, nature of  injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant  and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.
 Decisions of this Court and the High Courts contain Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
11  necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if  necessary. What usually poses some difficulty is the  assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of  permanent disability--Item (ii)(a). We are concerned  with that assessment in this case. 
 Assessment of future loss of earnings due to permanent  disability  8. Disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to  perform an activity in the manner considered normal for  a human being. Permanent disability refers to the  residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the  body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment  and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily  improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for  the remainder life of the injured. Temporary disability  refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the  body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist  at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation. 
 Permanent disability can be either partial or total. 
 Partial permanent disability refers to a person's  inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions  that he could perform before the accident, though he is  able to perform some of them and is still able to engage  in some gainful activity. Total permanent disability  refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or  employment related activities as a result of the accident. 
 The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor  accident injuries, are of a much wider range when  compared to the physical disabilities which are  enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 17 of 35  Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full  Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act", for  short). But if any of the disabilities enumerated in  Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of  injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be  permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming  compensation. 
 9. The percentage of permanent disability is expressed  by the doctors with reference to the whole body, or more  often than not, with reference to a particular limb. 
 When a disability certificate states that the injured has  suffered permanent disability to an extent of 45% of the  left lower limb, it is not the same as 45% permanent  disability with reference to the whole body. The extent  of disability of a limb (or part of the body) expressed in  terms of a percentage of the total functions of that limb ,
 obviously cannot be assumed to be the extent of  disability of the whole body. If there is 60% permanent  disability of the right hand and 80% permanent  disability of left leg, it does not mean that the extent of Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/
12  permanent disability with reference to the whole body is  140% (that is 80% plus 60%). If different parts of the  body have suffered different percentages of disabilities,
 the sum total thereof expressed in terms of the  permanent disability with reference to the whole body  cannot obviously exceed 100%. 
 10. Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability  as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation  under the head of loss of future earnings would depend  upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability  on his earning capacity. The Tribunal should not  mechanically apply the percentage of permanent  disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of  earning capacity. In most of the cases, the percentage of  economic loss, that is, the percentage of loss of earning  capacity , arising from a permanent disability will be  different from the percentage of permanent disability. 
 Some Tribunals wrongly assume that in all cases, a  particular extent (percentage) of permanent disability  would result in a corresponding loss of earning MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 18 of 35  capacity, and consequently, if the evidence produced  show 45% as the permanent disability, will hold that  there is 45% loss of future earning capacity. In most of  the cases , equating the extent (percentage) of loss of  earning capacity to the extent (percentage) of  permanent disability will result in award of either too  low or too high a compensation. 
 11. What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the  effect of the permanent disability on the earning  capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of  earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the  income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to  arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the  standard multiplier method used to determine loss of  dependency). We may however note that in some cases,
